To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) salinity shock is a major stress factor for the Pacific oyster Crassotrea gigas; (2) salinity shock may lead to mortality of oysters that are not infected with OsHV-1; and (3) salinity shock increases the susceptibility of oysters to infection by OsHV-1, which is a major pathogen in this species.
